problems: The blind guess captures the boat, the curved hull and the wavy water line, but not the boatman, who is the main subject. The figure reads mainly as a wedge-shaped hull, so the title's human subject is lost.

The hull is angular rather than curved. The top edge runs as a straight gold line from the raised stern-post tip (65387, ~132,352) to the bow tip (60320, ~315,428), and the stern rises in a sharp corner at 64820 (~163,411) instead of a smooth sweep.

The boatman is too small and cramped against the hull. His head (58758, ~383,307) sits in a tight blue loop, and the hip (59072, ~369,347), elbow (60009, ~335,326) and shell coin (60718, ~310,298) form a small stick figure, so the arm and body do not read as a silhouette.

The stars sit roughly on the right parts: the coin is in the open palm to the left, the elbow bends the arm out left, the hip is at the cloak's side, and the keel is at the hull bottom. The figure is upright, with the hull below and the man above.
The labels overlap and are clipped at the frame edge, and the blue silhouette outline runs under the gold lines. This makes it unclear which contour is the actual silhouette.
The wavy waterline at about y=483 (x 190 to 290) is detached from the hull keel at 61585 (~275,470), so the hull seems to float rather than sit in the water.
